Questions venue owners often ask

What happens on the first call?

We discuss the venue, audience, possible dates and what you want the event to achieve. It is an initial conversation, not a commitment to host an event.

What would the venue be responsible for?

A venue commonly provides the space, its agreed hospitality offer and an on-site contact. Staffing, suppliers and operating roles depend on the event and are agreed in advance.

How do we decide whether to proceed?

If there may be a fit, the next step can be a written outline of scope, date, budget and responsibilities. Nothing is booked, promoted or spent until both sides agree.

What will it cost?

There is no single rate for every event. The estimate depends on the format, production needs, suppliers and each party’s role. Fees, costs and terms are set out before anything is confirmed.

How are tickets and revenue handled?

There is no standard revenue split. Ticket price, inclusions, platform and fees, costs and revenue allocation are agreed before promotion. Ticket sales and attendance are not guaranteed.

What capacity can we plan for?

We plan within the venue’s permitted safe capacity, layout, service model and event format. Actual attendance cannot be guaranteed.

How much lead time is needed?

Timing depends on the date, supplier availability, production needs, any permissions and promotion. We agree a realistic schedule once those details are clear rather than promise a standard lead time.
